entries.label: Emerging markets: not less risky
entries.summary: Emerging markets carry more political risk in a tougher growth environment.
entries.quote: For the past four years, we've been uncritically thankful for the emerging markets.

entries.label: China vs information
entries.summary: The flow of information challenges China's government.
entries.quote: Take a serious look at China and the risks come faster than you can process: labor scarcity, pensions, inefficiency of state owned enterprises, conflicts in the East and South China Seas, clean water availability, clean air, food and commodity scarcity (and prices).

entries.label: Arab summer
entries.summary: The Arab Spring turns into a period of conflict.
entries.quote: It was barely more than a year ago that we were talking hopefully about an Arab spring.

entries.label: Washington Politics
entries.summary: US political dysfunction threatens a year that could bring reform.
entries.quote: 2013 should be a year for reform progress and renewed economic dynamism in the United States.

entries.label: JIBs - Japan, Israel and Britain
entries.summary: Japan, Israel and Britain lose out from current global trends.
entries.quote: There are three current global trends that matter most: China is rising, the Middle East is exploding, and Europe is muddling through.

entries.label: Europe
entries.summary: Eurozone financial risk falls but political risks remain.
entries.quote: The risks generated by the European financial crisis were substantially lowered when, in late summer, German chancellor Angela Merkel rejected the hardline approach of the German Bundesbank leadership and endorsed ECB President Mario Draghi’s commitment to buy the bonds of ailing eurozone countries.

entries.label: East Asian geopolitics
entries.summary: East Asian geopolitical risk grows in a new way.
entries.quote: Geopolitical risk will continue growing in East Asia in 2013 in a new, and potentially more dangerous, way.

entries.label: Iran
entries.summary: Pressure on Iran continues though a strike in 2013 is very unlikely.
entries.quote: It never fails, we give a speech and we get the question—when is the United States or, failing that, Israel going to bomb Iran? It's very unlikely, especially in 2013.

entries.label: India
entries.summary: Politics intrudes on India's economic success story.
entries.quote: India in 2013 will be one of the prime examples of the intrusion of political factors into what had been until recently seen as a long-term economic success story.

entries.label: South Africa
entries.summary: South Africa shows rising political risk despite African growth.
entries.quote: Sub-Saharan Africa, more than any other region, epitomizes the paradox of the shift in economic dynamism to the emerging markets and the significant increase in political risk.

entries.label: Geopolitics of energy
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect Middle East turmoil to drive energy prices up.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Global protectionism
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect a rise in protectionism.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Radicalism in the developed world
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect class conflict to destabilise developed countries.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: European separatism
entries.summary: Eurasia Group sees almost no chance that Catalan, Scottish or Belgian separatism becomes a crisis in 2013.
entries.quote: But there is almost no chance that any of these issues grows into an actual crisis in 2013.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: North Korea
entries.summary: Eurasia Group says it cannot know what is happening in North Korea under Kim Jong-un.
entries.quote: Sometimes...you just can’t know what's happening. Looking at North Korea this year, that's really the case.
entries.note: Printed as '? - North Korea'; not ranked.
